newsitem.title: ESTONIA: ANALYSIS-ESTONIA SHARES SEEN BOOSTED BY BANK RESULTS.
newsitem.headline: ANALYSIS-ESTONIA SHARES SEEN BOOSTED BY BANK RESULTS.

text.p: Positive first-half bank results are expected to keep the Estonian bourse on track for more gains although some say prices may be knocked by a short-term correction after recent gains, analysts said on Wednesday.
Although Estonian price/earnings ratios make shares seem more expensive than in Lithuania and Latvia, analysts said Estonian stocks still offered better returns.
"The banks' first half year results were good and this should set the bourse up for good returns in the coming months," one dealer said.
Shares rose again on Wednesday, breaching the 300-level for the first time as it gained 0.84 percent to 300.22.
Bank shares are the most traded on the bourse, with the Baltics' biggest bank Hansapank , leading the pack. The other major traded banks are Uhispank , Tallinna Pank, Hoiupank and Forekspank .
"Most bank results were quite strong but Hansa and Hoiupank's stood out," said Tallinna Pank analyst Sander Danil.
All banks are expected to raise their profit forecasts, with Hoiupank and Hansapank to show most gains.
"The results were good and the first half of the year is usually hardest," said Katrin Kaarli, analyst from Hansapank.
"Investors are now convinced the banks' managers can manage and widen the product range," she added, noting that banks were viewed positively and were attracting more long-term investors.

There are also expectations for growth despite an average price/earning ratio for all companies listed on the main list of the bourse of 10.7 which makes some say that compared with the bourses in Latvia and Lithuania, shares are overvalued.
Hansapank is the most expensive stock with a P/E ratio of 15.9 and Hoiupank follows at 12.6.
"If you compare the banking sectors then Estonian shares are 30 percent higher than Latvia and Lithuania," Danil added.
But Kaarli said that Estonian stocks could be considered cheaper as they brought higher returns due to better management, more reliable information and better trading systems.
Analysts were divided over the short-term and whether there would be a correction in the near future after recent gains.
The market has been setting new highs for the past three days as bank results have come flooding in.
"Looking to the end of this month, I think some prices will come down as the market under goes a correction," Danil said.
But Karli disagreed.
"We don't really expect a correction, the good results support the higher market levels," Kaarli said.
If there is a correction, both dealers and analysts said they expected it to be quick.
"It won't last long as strong growth is expected in the autumn, so it should recover quickly," Danil added.
"The bourse is expected to rise in the autumn, not as much as last year, but a solid gain," one dealer said.
